To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chitosan/haluronic acid nanoparticles can be formulated by simple mixing of thioketal functionalized chitosan and hyaluronic acid, and the resultant NPs are responsive to oxidative stress and pH.
we developed chitosan/hylauronic acid nanocapsules with high loading capacity and controlled release of quarcetin, curcmin and NGF.

we have developed a simple method to prepare chitosan/hylauronic acid nanoparticles that respond to oxidative stress in the tumor microenvironment and can be used to deliver small drug molecules and protein therapeutics to the tumor site and peripheral nerve tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a facile and efficient approach to develop autogenous responsive nanocarriers for the efficient delivery of therapeutic molecules to specific sites.
the development of a versatile platform for the delivery of small drug molecules as well as proteins to the target cells and tissues.
the development of a facile and versatile method of designing autogenous stimuli responsive NPs that can be used to deliver small molecules and protein based therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this facile strategy to formulate autogenous stimuli responsive nanoparticles can be used to develop a wide range of nanomedicine formulations for the treatment of diseases.
this study demonstrates a facile strategy to formulate autogenous stimuli responsive nanoparticles for delivery of small molecules and proteins to the target site with high efficiency.
the facile design of chitosan/hylauronic acid nanostructures is an efficient and effective approach for delivery of small molecules and proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be used to develop a wide range of stimuli responsive nanoparticles for efficient delivery of small molecules and protein based drugs.

we report the facile fabrication of autogenous stimuli sensitive chitosan/hylauronic acid nanoparticles with high drug loading capacity, which can efficiently deliver small drug molecules and protein under specific endogenous stimuli.
we have developed an efficient and facile method to design autogenous responsive chitosan nanoparticles with high drug loading capacity for the delivery of small molecules and proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single thioketal based small organic molecule can be used to design multifunctional chitosan based nanocarriers for efficient and controlled delivery of small and large molecules.
thioketal based chitosan/hyuluronan NPs can be easily fabricated with multiple stimuli responsiveness for the delivery of small molecules and proteins to the target sites.
the proposed nanocarriers can be readily assembled from low molecular weight biopolymers and can be used to deliver both small molecules and proteins in response to endogenous triggers.
